Cyber Attack Disrupts Irish Retailers' IT Systems, Stores Remain Closed

DUBLIN, June 8 – Major retail chains in Ireland are facing widespread disruption after a sophisticated cyber attack struck key IT systems overnight, forcing the closure of hundreds of stores and impeding online sales, industry sources said Saturday.

The incident, described by company officials as a ransomware attack, has affected multiple firms, including grocery, clothing, and electronics retailers. Among those impacted is O’Shea’s Retail Group, which confirmed its 128 outlets nationwide were unable to process transactions or access stock management systems.

“Unfortunately, all of our stores remain closed while we work with cybersecurity experts to contain the incident and restore operations,” said O’Shea’s spokesperson Claire Doran. “We apologise to our customers and appreciate their patience.”

The Irish Retail Federation said at least six major chains have temporarily shut their physical locations, with point-of-sale terminals offline and staff unable to access payroll or scheduling platforms. “We are deeply concerned for the 12,000 workers currently affected, many of whom have been sent home until further notice,” said Federation CEO Michael Reilly.

Retailers have also suspended click-and-collect and home delivery services as e-commerce websites remain inaccessible or operate in limited mode. “We are aware of the significant disruption this is causing ahead of a busy weekend,” said Reilly. “Our members are working around the clock to mitigate the impact.”

IT security analysts say the attack appears coordinated and targeted at retailers’ central databases. “This is one of the most disruptive incidents the Irish retail sector has seen,” said Siobhan Kelly, a cybersecurity consultant. “Recovery could take days, depending on the extent of the systems affected.”

The National Cyber Security Centre confirmed it is assisting affected firms. The source and full scope of the attack remain under investigation.
